## Part 2: What makes a vulnerability get exploited?

```{r}
#| label: p2-setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
source(here::here("R", "theme_dataforge.R"))

p2_v <- readRDS(here::here("data", "processed", "vulns.rds")) |>
  filter(pub_year >= 2016, !is.na(cvss_score)) |>
  mutate(cwe_top15 = fct_lump_n(cwe, n =15))

p2_rate <- function(var) {
  p2_v |>
    group_by({{ var }}) |>
    summarise(n = n(), rate = 100 * mean(exploited), .groups = "drop")
}

p2_n       <- nrow(p2_v)
p2_n_exp   <- sum(p2_v$exploited)
p2_overall <- 100 * mean(p2_v$exploited)

p2_sev  <- p2_rate(severity)
p2_crit <- p2_sev$rate[p2_sev$severity == "CRITICAL"]
p2_med  <- p2_sev$rate[p2_sev$severity == "MEDIUM"]

p2_rce     <- p2_rate(says_rce)
p2_rce_yes <- p2_rce$rate[p2_rce$says_rce]
p2_rce_no  <- p2_rce$rate[!p2_rce$says_rce]

p2_cwe_names <- c(
  "CWE-78"  = "OS command injection",       "CWE-22"  = "Path traversal",
  "CWE-787" = "Out-of-bounds write",        "CWE-416" = "Use after free",
  "CWE-20"  = "Improper input validation",  "CWE-119" = "Buffer overflow",
  "CWE-284" = "Improper access control",    "CWE-89"  = "SQL injection",
  "CWE-74"  = "Injection (general)",        "CWE-200" = "Information exposure",
  "CWE-125" = "Out-of-bounds read",         "CWE-862" = "Missing authorisation",
  "CWE-79"  = "Cross-site scripting (XSS)", "CWE-352" = "Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)",
  "CWE-476" = "NULL pointer dereference"
)

p2_cwe <- p2_rate(cwe_top15) |>
  filter(!is.na(cwe_top15), cwe_top15 != "Other") |>
  mutate(label = paste(cwe_top15, p2_cwe_names[as.character(cwe_top15)]))
p2_cwe78   <- p2_cwe$rate[p2_cwe$cwe_top15 == "CWE-78"]
p2_cwe79   <- p2_cwe$rate[p2_cwe$cwe_top15 == "CWE-79"]
p2_cwe79_n <- p2_cwe$n[p2_cwe$cwe_top15 == "CWE-79"]

p2_wil <- wilcox.test(cvss_score ~ exploited, data = p2_v)
p2_scores <- p2_v |> group_by(exploited) |> summarise(median = median(cvss_score))
p2_med_exp <- p2_scores$median[p2_scores$exploited]
p2_med_not <- p2_scores$median[!p2_scores$exploited]

p2_assoc <- function(var) {
  tab  <- table(p2_v[[var]], p2_v$exploited)
  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab))
  tibble(feature  = var,
         p_value  = test$p.value,
         cramers_v = unname(sqrt(test$statistic / (sum(tab) * (min(dim(tab)) - 1)))))
}

p2_tests <- map_dfr(c("severity", "attack_vector", "privileges_required",
                      "user_interaction", "says_rce", "cwe_group", "vendor_group"),
                    p2_assoc)
p2_v_max <- max(p2_tests$cramers_v)
p2_p_max <- max(p2_tests$p_value)

p2_fit <- glm(exploited ~ cvss_score + attack_vector + privileges_required +
                user_interaction + says_rce + says_auth_bypass + vendor_group,
              data = p2_v, family = binomial)

p2_odds <- tidy(p2_fit) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
         low  = exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
         high = exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error))

p2_or <- function(t) p2_odds$odds_ratio[p2_odds$term == t]
p2_or_auth   <- p2_or("says_auth_bypassTRUE")
p2_or_cvss   <- p2_or("cvss_score")
p2_or_ui     <- p2_or("user_interactionREQUIRED")
p2_or_prnone <- p2_or("privileges_requiredNONE")
p2_or_ms     <- p2_or("vendor_groupmicrosoft")
p2_or_cisco  <- p2_or("vendor_groupcisco")

p2_pr <- p2_v |>
  group_by(privileges_required) |>
  summarise(rate = 100 * mean(exploited), median = median(cvss_score))
p2_pr_none <- p2_pr |> filter(privileges_required == "NONE")
p2_pr_high <- p2_pr |> filter(privileges_required == "HIGH")

p2_zero_vendors <- p2_v |>
  group_by(vendor_group) |>
  summarise(exploited = sum(exploited)) |>
  filter(exploited == 0) |>
  pull(vendor_group)

p2_nice_names <- c(
  "vendor_group"         = "",
  "attack_vector"        = "Attack vector: ",
  "privileges_required"  = "Privileges needed: ",
  "user_interaction"     = "User interaction: ",
  "says_auth_bypassTRUE" = "Mentions authentication bypass",
  "says_rceTRUE"         = "Mentions remote code execution",
  "cvss_score"           = "CVSS score (each extra point)"
)

p2_odds_plot <- p2_odds |>
  filter(!term %in% paste0("vendor_group", p2_zero_vendors)) |>
  mutate(label = str_replace_all(term, p2_nice_names),
         is_vendor = str_starts(term, "vendor_group"))
```

Critical vulnerabilities were `r round(p2_crit / p2_med)` times more likely to be exploited than Medium ones (`r round(p2_crit, 2)`% against `r round(p2_med, 2)`%, @fig-p2-severity). We compared the `r scales::comma(p2_n)` CVEs published from 2016 onwards that have a CVSS score. Of these, `r scales::comma(p2_n_exp)` (`r round(p2_overall, 2)`%) are in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, which is how we label a vulnerability as exploited.

```{r}
#| label: fig-p2-severity
#| fig-cap: "Share of CVEs exploited in each CVSS severity band, with the number of CVEs in each band."
#| echo: false
p2_sev |>
  filter(severity != "NONE") |>
  mutate(severity = factor(severity, levels = c("LOW", "MEDIUM", "HIGH", "CRITICAL"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = severity, y = rate)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(rate, 2), "%  (n = ", scales::comma(n), ")")),
            vjust = -0.5) +
  labs(title = paste0("Critical CVEs are exploited ", round(p2_crit / p2_med),
                      " times as often as Medium ones"),
       x = "CVSS severity", y = "Exploited (%)") +
  theme_dataforge()
```

Descriptions that mention remote code execution were the next clearest signal: those CVEs were exploited at `r round(p2_rce_yes, 2)`%, about `r round(p2_rce_yes / p2_rce_no)` times the rate of the rest (`r round(p2_rce_no, 2)`%). The type of weakness mattered too (@fig-p2-cwe). OS command injection (CWE-78) was exploited at `r round(p2_cwe78, 2)`%, while cross-site scripting (CWE-79), the most common weakness type with `r scales::comma(p2_cwe79_n)` CVEs, was exploited at only `r round(p2_cwe79, 2)`%.

```{r}
#| label: fig-p2-cwe
#| fig-cap: "Exploit rate for the 15 most common weakness types (CWE). The dashed line is the average for all CVEs."
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
p2_cwe |>
  ggplot(aes(x = rate, y = fct_reorder(label, rate))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = p2_overall, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = p2_overall, y = 1, hjust = -0.1,
           label = paste0("average ", round(p2_overall, 2), "%")) +
  labs(title = "OS command injection (CWE-78) is the most exploited weakness type",
       x = "Exploited (%)", y = "Weakness type (CWE)") +
  theme_dataforge()
```

These differences are real but small. Exploited CVEs had a median CVSS score of `r p2_med_exp`, against `r p2_med_not` for the rest (Wilcoxon test, p `r format.pval(p2_wil$p.value, eps = 0.001)`), and chi-square tests linked every feature we tested to exploitation (all p-values below `r signif(p2_p_max, 1)`). With over 300,000 CVEs, however, almost any difference counts as "significant", so we also measured how strong each link is with Cramér's V, which runs from 0 (no link) to 1 (a perfect link). The strongest link was only `r round(p2_v_max, 2)`, so no single feature predicts exploitation well on its own.

Looking at all the features together in one logistic regression model, which measures how much each feature changes the odds of exploitation while the others are held fixed, a mention of authentication bypass had the strongest effect: it multiplied the odds by `r round(p2_or_auth, 1)` (@fig-p2-odds-features). An odds ratio above 1 means more likely to be exploited, and below 1 means less likely. Each extra CVSS point multiplied the odds by `r round(p2_or_cvss, 2)`, and needing a user to click something lowered them (`r round(p2_or_ui, 2)`). Among vendors, Microsoft and Cisco CVEs had `r round(p2_or_ms, 1)` and `r round(p2_or_cisco, 1)` times the odds of Adobe's, the comparison vendor, which is itself often exploited (@fig-p2-odds-vendors).

One result differs from the rate tables. Bugs that need no privileges were exploited more often than those needing high privileges (`r round(p2_pr_none$rate, 2)`% against `r round(p2_pr_high$rate, 2)`%), but in the model their odds ratio is `r round(p2_or_prnone, 2)`. The CVSS formula already gives these bugs higher scores (median `r format(p2_pr_none$median, nsmall = 1)` against `r format(p2_pr_high$median, nsmall = 1)`), so once the score is held fixed, needing no privileges adds no extra risk.

```{r}
#| label: fig-p2-odds-features
#| fig-cap: "Odds ratios with 95% intervals for the technical features, from one logistic regression model. Compared with: adjacent network, high privileges, no user interaction."
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
p2_odds_plot |>
  filter(!is_vendor) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = odds_ratio, y = fct_reorder(label, odds_ratio))) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Authentication-bypass bugs have nearly 3 times the odds of exploitation",
       subtitle = "Above 1 = more likely to be exploited, below 1 = less likely",
       x = "Odds ratio (log scale)", y = "Feature") +
  theme_dataforge()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-p2-odds-vendors
#| fig-cap: "Odds ratios with 95% intervals for vendors, from the same model, compared with Adobe. Only vendors clearly different from Adobe are shown; vendors with no exploited CVEs are left out."
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
p2_odds_plot |>
  filter(is_vendor, low > 1 | high < 1) |>
  mutate(label = str_to_title(label) |> str_replace("Ibm", "IBM")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = odds_ratio, y = fct_reorder(label, odds_ratio))) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3)) +
  labs(title = "Microsoft and Cisco CVEs have over 3 times Adobe's odds of exploitation",
       subtitle = "Above 1 = more likely to be exploited than Adobe, below 1 = less likely",
       x = "Odds ratio (log scale)", y = "Vendor") +
  theme_dataforge()
```
